title: Design a Family-Friendly Listing Classifier
prompt: Design a classifier or filter that helps guests find family-friendly homes. Define what the label means, how you would learn it from available data, and how you would evaluate and use the result. Discuss noisy labels and new listings.

response.placeholder: State your assumptions, then explain your approach and tradeoffs.
response.reference_answer:
This is a practice answer outline, not a reported interview solution.

Define suitability for a specified family use case before choosing a model. Distinguish verified amenities from subjective review evidence, and use reviewed examples to estimate weak-label error. Start with a calibrated tabular baseline using time-valid listing and permitted trip signals; add text or image features only if they improve held-out performance. Avoid treating missing evidence as proof of suitability.

Evaluate precision, recall and calibration, including new listings and relevant listing/guest slices. Choose a threshold based on the cost of false assurances versus missed options. Validate online booking outcomes alongside complaints, refunds and user satisfaction. Monitor label drift and provide a correction path.
